'''Jasjeet''' "'''Jas'''" '''Singh Sekhon''' is a [[Data science|data scientist]], [[political scientist]], and [[Statistics|statistician]] at [[Yale University]]. Sekhon is the Eugene Meyer Professor at [[Yale University]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Jasjeet Sekhon |url=https://statistics.yale.edu/people/jasjeet-sekhon |website=Department of Statistics and Data Science |publisher=Yale University |access-date=4 June 2021}}</ref> a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]],<ref name="asa">{{cite web |title=Jas Sekhon Selected as a Fellow of the American Statistical Association |url=https://statistics.yale.edu/news/jas-sekhon-selected-fellow-american-statistical-association |website=Department of Statistics and Data Science |publisher=Yale University |access-date=4 June 2021}}</ref> and a fellow of the [[Society for Political Methodology]].<ref name="spm">{{cite web |title=Fellows |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/membership/spm/about-us/fellows/fellows-2019 |website=Cambridge University Press |publisher=Society for Political Methodology |access-date=4 June 2021 |language=en}}</ref> Sekhon's primary research interests lie in [[causal inference]], [[machine learning]], and their intersection.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jasjeet Sekhon|url=https://statistics.yale.edu/people/jasjeet-sekhon|website=Jasjeet Sekhon|access-date=3 June 2021}}</ref> He has also published research on their application in various fields including [[voting behavior]], online experimentation, [[epidemiology]], and [[medicine]].

==Biography==
Sekhon graduated with a B.A. from the [[University of British Columbia]]. In 1999, he earned a Ph.D. at [[Cornell University]].<ref name="spm" /><ref name="fas">{{cite web |title=Jasjeet Sekhon |url=https://fas.yale.edu/book/new-ladder-faculty-2020-2021/jasjeet-sekhon |website=New Ladder Faculty (2020-2021) |publisher=Yale University |access-date=4 June 2021}}</ref>

Sekhon's career in academia began in 1999, when he became an assistant professor at [[Harvard University]]. He stayed at Harvard until 2005 when he moved to [[UC Berkeley]]. At Berkeley, he was appointed as the Robson Professor of Political Science and Statistics in 2014.<ref name="cv">{{cite web |url=https://jsekhon.com/SekhonCV.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae}}</ref> In 2018, he accepted a non-academic position at [[Bridgewater Associates]], where he was chief scientist and head of AI/ML.<ref name="BI">{{cite web |url=https://www.parsintl.com/eprints/119288.pdf |title=How 9 hedge funds including Bridgewater, Millennium and AQR are thinking about AI -- and the 11 experts leading the charge|publisher=Business Insider}}</ref><ref name="BI0">{{cite web |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/bridgewater-building-ai-fund-machine-learning-greg-jensen-2023-11 |title=One of Bridgewater's top investors explains why the world's largest hedge fund is handing the investment process over to AI in a new fund|publisher=Business Insider}}</ref> In 2020, he left Berkeley to join [[Yale University]], where he was appointed Meyer Professor of Political Science and Statistics and Data Science in 2021.<ref name="yalenews">{{cite web |url=https://news.yale.edu/2021/04/12/sekhon-named-meyer-professor-political-science-and-statistics-and-data |title=Sekhon named Meyer Professor of Political Science and Statistics and Data |publisher=YaleNews}}</ref> He was named a fellow of the Society for Political Methodology in 2019<ref name="spm" /> and a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] in 2021.<ref name=asa /> In March 2026, Sekhon joined [[Google DeepMind]] as its [[chief strategy officer]] after leaving his executive role at Bridgewater, while also joining its board.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/bridgewaters-chief-scientist-sekhon-join-googles-deepmind-ai-unit-2026-03-18/|title=Bridgewater's chief scientist Sekhon to join Google's DeepMind AI unit|last=Sen|first=Anirban|date=March 18, 2026|work=Reuters}}</ref>

Sekhon has authored or co-authored dozens of journal articles and several widely used software packages. The topics of his scholarship include experimental research methods, [[machine learning]] for estimating causal effects, election fraud, and [[Matching (statistics)|matching]]. His research has been widely cited.<ref name="google scholar">{{cite web |title="Jasjeet S. Sekhon - Google Scholar" |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=FjdjShkAAAAJ&hl=en |website=Jasjeet S. Sekhon - Google Scholar |publisher=Google Scholar |access-date=28 November 2021}}</ref>

==Research==
Sekhon is best known for his research in [[causal inference]] and [[machine learning]]. His early research on causal inference focused on the role of matching, but he later wrote an article pointing out that matching is unable to address many of the problems (particularly the selection on observables assumption) that its proponents assume. Nevertheless, his Genetic Matching algorithm remains one of his most highly cited articles.<ref name="google scholar" /> As of 2021, his research focuses on developing interpretable and credible machine learning methods for estimating causal relationships.<ref name="fas" />

One of Sekhon's first publications, a journal article in ''Digestive Diseases and Sciences'', presented a novel treatment, [[glucocorticoid]], for a rare disease that he suffered. Sekhon himself was the first case described in the article.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sekhon |first1=Jasjeet |last2=Chung |first2=Raymond |last3=Epstein |first3=Mark |last4=Kaplan |first4=Marshal |title=Steroid-Responsive (Autoimmune?) Sclerosing Cholangitis |journal=Digestive Diseases and Sciences |date=2005 |volume=50 |issue=10 |pages=1838–1843|doi=10.1007/s10620-005-2948-3 |pmid=16187184 |s2cid=15494269 }}</ref>
